verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 56.46
verses.english: Linked Discourses 56.46

verses.pali: 5. Papātavagga
verses.english: 5. A Cliff

verses.pali: Andhakārasutta
verses.english: Darkness

verses.pali: “Atthi, bhikkhave, lokantarikā aghā asaṁvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā, yatthamimesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ evaṁmahiddhikānaṁ evaṁ mahānubhāvānaṁ ābhāya nānubhontī”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, the boundless gloom of interstellar space is so utterly dark that even the luminosity of the moon and the sun, so mighty and powerful, makes no impression.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, one of the mendicants asked the Buddha,

verses.pali: “mahā vata so, bhante, andhakāro, sumahā vata so, bhante, andhakāro.
verses.english: “Sir, that darkness really is mighty, so very mighty.

verses.pali: Atthi nu kho, bhante, etamhā andhakārā añño andhakāro mahantataro ca bhayānakataro cā”ti?
verses.english: Is there any other darkness more mighty and terrifying than this one?”

verses.pali: “Atthi kho, bhikkhu, etamhā andhakārā añño andhakāro mahantataro ca bhayānakataro cā”ti.
verses.english: “There is, mendicant.”

verses.pali: “Katamo pana, bhante, etamhā andhakārā añño andhakāro mahantataro ca bhayānakataro cā”ti?
verses.english: “But sir, what is it?”

verses.pali: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhu, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti,
verses.english: “There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: te jātisaṁvattanikesu saṅkhāresu abhiramanti …pe…
verses.english: They take pleasure in choices that lead to rebirth …

verses.pali: abhiratā …pe… abhisaṅkharonti …pe…
verses.english: They continue to make such choices …

verses.pali: abhisaṅkharitvā jātandhakārampi papatanti, jarandhakārampi papatanti, maraṇandhakārampi papatanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsandhakārampi papatanti.
verses.english: Having made such choices, they fall into the darkness of rebirth, old age, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: Te na parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
verses.english: They’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: ‘Na parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhu, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti,
verses.english: There are ascetics and brahmins who truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: te jātisaṁvattanikesu saṅkhāresu nābhiramanti …pe…
verses.english: They don’t take pleasure in choices that lead to rebirth …

verses.pali: anabhiratā …pe… nābhisaṅkharonti …pe…
verses.english: They stop making such choices …

verses.pali: anabhisaṅkharitvā jātandhakārampi nappapatanti, jarandhakārampi nappapatanti, maraṇandhakārampi nappapatanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsandhakārampi nappapatanti.
verses.english: Having stopped making such choices, they don’t fall into the darkness of rebirth, old age, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: Te parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
verses.english: They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: ‘Parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
